rules.covers: error handling: every outbound request sits in a try block (template rule, statement list widened from api.request to the other outbound statements named in the skill)
timeout: every outbound request has a timeout of at most 30 seconds (template rule, statement list widened)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: error handling must actually do something (fallback, alert) rather than just exist
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists: containment only confirms a try_catch wraps the call; an empty catch passes

ask_parts_not_covered.part: app should not hang as a whole when a vendor is down (concurrency, retry loops)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: a per-call cap does not bound retry loops such as the retry_failed_webhooks task's while loop

ask_parts_not_covered.part: calls via db.external.* and ai.external.mcp.* cannot time out
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists: those statements take no timeout param, so no rule can bound them

assumptions: The ask 'any external API call' maps to outbound statements api.request, stream.from_request, webflow.request, api.microservice and api.lambda, from the skill's statement names list.
A 30-second maximum is an acceptable reading of the template's 'time out quickly' summary; the customer did not give a number.
Omitted timeouts are judged at the 10-second default per the check's limits note, so they pass SEC-013. I did not add a min or require-explicit rule.
Two policies, one per template, because the skill says one policy per template when starting from templates. The ask is one goal, so this is a judgement call.
api.microservice and api.lambda exist as statement names in this platform version (taken from the skill text); neither appears in the workspace.
Advisory enforcement, as the template prescribes, since the customer did not ask for blocking.
confusions: The template SEC-013 description says 'times out within 30 seconds' but the check's limits say an omitted timeout is judged at 10 seconds. The product should say plainly whether a call with no timeout counts as having one. As written, a call with no timeout passes, which may not be what a customer asking for timeouts expects.

The template's 'Fill' column says nothing for both templates, but the check's statement list is a fixed set in the template. The skill does not say whether widening a template's statement list is an allowed change or counts as changing the template. I widened it because the ask says 'any external API call'.

The skill says one policy per template, but the customer asked for one goal (external calls are safe). Combining the two templates into one policy would need a new key, which the skill only allows when no template covers the request. Unclear which to prefer.
xano policy parse's summary output drops the severity line, while -o json keeps it. Easy to misread as severity being lost.

The skill's external-statement list includes api.microservice and api.lambda with timeout params, but the SEC-013 and LOG-010 templates do not name them. I could not verify these statement names against the workspace or the catalogue's check parameters beyond the skill text.
wished_for: A template or check that verifies the catch block does something (not empty, calls a function or throws).
A policy recipe for 'every outbound call', listing the full outbound statement set once, so the set is not rebuilt from prose.
Whether a missing timeout should fail the rule, or a documented example of requiring an explicit timeout (min bound on a param that may be absent).
Confirmation that api.microservice and api.lambda are accepted statement names, e.g. an example in the catalogue.
why_confidence: Both rules parse with no rule warnings, and the timeout and try-wrapper parts are directly checkable. The policies do not prove the error handling is meaningful or that the app will not hang as a whole, and I have not run xano policy evaluate (forbidden here), so the findings predicted in the reply are from reading the code, not from the platform.
